questions.question: The faster you drink:

options.text: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
The faster your body removes the alcohol.
The less you feel the effects of alcohol.
The less likely you are to get pulled over.

questions.correctAnswerText: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: The faster you drink, the more alcohol builds up in your body. It is never safe to drive after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Protect only your eyes.
Work as well as a face shield.
Protect your face as well as a windshield.
Protect your entire face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protect only your eyes.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes, not the rest of your face. A face shield protects your whole face and is better than goggles. A windshield does not replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if the clothing is loose and flaps in the wind.
Yes, if you wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if you wear a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Proper clothing can reduce injury in a crash. Wear a sturdy jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs completely and fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be reduced by:

options.text: Wearing a helmet.
Wearing a leather jacket.
Using the rear brake only.
Wearing goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing a helmet.
questions.explanation: A good helmet greatly reduces the risk of head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Stop completely.
Speed up to create distance between you and them.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them ahead of you. If it is safe, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only increases danger and may cause them to tailgate you at a higher speed.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, the operator should:

options.text: Keep a longer distance behind other vehicles.
Increase their speed.
Let air out of the tires to handle the extra weight.
Not warn passengers about dangers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger on board. You should keep a larger safety distance behind other vehicles when carrying another person.

questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat because:

options.text: You can jump off if you need to.
Your legs can absorb the shock.
Other drivers can see you better.
You can see the surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your legs absorb some of the impact force. This keeps the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: A motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More visible than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flashing your brake light before slowing down or stopping helps other drivers see that you are braking.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Not wear a jacket in warm weather.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
Wear shorts in warm weather.
Not worry about long shoelaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of sturdy material, even in warm weather. A jacket helps protect you and prevents dehydration. Always wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: When preparing to pass, you should ride in the left portion of your lane because:

options.text: It improves what you can see ahead.
It limits what you can see ahead.
It makes it harder to see past the vehicle.
It allows the other driver to speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It improves what you can see ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This improves your view ahead and makes other drivers in the passing lane more likely to see you.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Leave space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Not use your rearview mirrors to check traffic behind you.
Look for chances to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or if a vehicle approaches quickly from behind.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.

options.text: Time
Coffee
Exercise
Fresh air

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol from your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot reduce your blood alcohol level. They may keep you awake, but they do not make you sober.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do to prevent injury when riding on a slippery surface?

options.text: Go faster.
Slow down.
Make sudden moves.
Ride on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, it is safest to reduce your speed. Sudden moves on slippery surfaces can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: Keep enough distance behind other vehicles to:

options.text: Give you time and space to see and react to dangers.
Allow you to tailgate.
Help traffic counters count you as a vehicle.
Encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you time and space to see and react to dangers.
questions.explanation: Keeping enough distance ensures you have space to stop or swerve if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. A space cushion also gives you a better view of road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: Drag your feet on the ground.
Point your toes downward.
Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
Keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Place your feet firmly on the footrests to keep good balance. Do not drag your feet or point them downward, as they could catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Go faster.
Use only the front brake.
Avoid sudden moves.
Ride on the shoulder to stay away from other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when needed, slow down, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, shaded spots, dirt, gravel, and bridges, as these surfaces offer less grip.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?

options.text: Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest
On the left handle grip
On the right handle grip

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it is done before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. It is also illegal to pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than usual.
Ride slower than usual.
Start slowing later than usual.
Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride slower than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and affects how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will accelerate slower, turn slower, and need more space to stop. Ride slowly, start braking sooner, keep a larger space cushion, and wait for bigger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: What should you check before riding your motorcycle?

options.text: Tire wear and tread
How much cushion your seat has
How shiny your paint is
Which way the wind is blowing

questions.correctAnswerText: Tire wear and tread
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, fluid levels, lights, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When choosing where to ride in your lane, you should think about:

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you
How many cars are ahead of you
Which position makes your trip shorter
Which position lets you pass more vehicles

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that makes you visible to other drivers. Also leave enough space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: Your body can only remove alcohol through:

options.text: Time
Drinking coffee
Exercise
A cold shower

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to get rid of alcohol. There is no way to speed up sobering up.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it hard to control your motorcycle and should not be used
Help other drivers notice you
Give you a better grip on the handlebars
Provide no protection at all

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is a lot of traffic
Dangerous for riders
Hard to understand
Safer than open roads

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous for riders
questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because many conflicts can happen between motorcyclists and other drivers there.
